_comment: Recording of live run 52 (status partial); the plan is the model's own words.

steps.message: Reviewing the intake and the question.

claims.text: The goal is to cut electricity bought from the grid by 30% by 2030 on a $500,000 capital budget for 2027. Efficiency alone does not reach it: the estimate is a 6.2% to 17.6% cut in grid use, which is 21% to 59% of the goal.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Rooftop solar cannot be sized yet. The roof is pitched, and the sizing rules do not allow a flat-roof estimate. A usable roof area verified by an engineer or roofer is needed first. Scenarios with solar (efficiency plus solar, and the full path with a battery) are not costed in this run and can be compared once that area is entered.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Whether solar is allowed on this roof is not settled by this plan. The building is a landmark, so a Landmarks Preservation Commission review is needed before any rooftop work, and a licensed structural engineer or architect must assess the roof. The roof cannot be certified from these records.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Jefferson Market Library (NYPL), 425 6th Avenue, Manhattan; a library built in 1877 with 19,800 sq ft of floor area as entered and a pitched roof of 7,020 sq ft as entered. The utility is Con Edison.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city record shows a landmark, three floors and one building on the lot, with a footprint of 7,019 sq ft. A footprint is the ground area under the building, not a measured roof. It is close to the 7,020 sq ft roof area entered, which is kept as the working figure and should still be confirmed by an engineer or roofer.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city lists this lot under a different street address, 421 Avenue of the Americas, instead of 425 6th Avenue. It may be another frontage of the same building. Please confirm.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city's energy report (Local Law 84, report year 2024) shows 18,643 sq ft of floor area, while 19,800 sq ft was entered and the city's tax-lot record also shows 19,800 sq ft. The entered 19,800 sq ft is used as the working figure. Please confirm which is right.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The intake lists no existing efficiency work and no existing renewables, so none were counted. If the library already has LED lighting, controls or solar, the savings and confidence here are lower.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Efficiency measures (LED lighting and controls) are assumed to save 10-20% of annual use. This is a planning estimate, not a cited benchmark and not a building model.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Prices are planning-level benchmarks, not quotes. Efficiency costs $1.17 to $4.02 per kWh saved per year for a standard package (the middle half of completed NYC public-sector projects, NYSERDA data). The efficiency savings percents are planning estimates, but only 62% to 88% of them is counted, because the City's audited projects delivered that share (NYC DCAS Local Law 87 report, fiscal 2022).
claims.label: ASSUMPTION
claims.units: USD per kWh saved per year

claims.text: The baseline is electricity bought from the grid: 268,331 kWh a year (kWh is energy over time). It matches the city's Local Law 84 report for 2024, 268,331 kWh, so the two agree.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city's report also shows 1,041,151 kBtu (thousand BTU) of natural gas, so heating appears to be gas. Gas use sits outside an electricity goal and is not counted in the 30% target.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: A standard efficiency package is estimated to save 16,637 to 47,226 kWh a year (6.2% to 17.6% of use). This counts only 62% to 88% of the predicted savings, because the City's own audited projects delivered that share. The underlying 10% to 20% savings are planning estimates.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: A building survey is needed to learn the lighting type, cooling type and controls, which the intake left blank. LED lighting is only worth including if it is not already installed.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Solar was not sized. The roof rules decided this, and it is not a data gap: the roof is pitched, so the flat-roof formulas for usable area, array size and output are not allowed. No array size, solar output or solar savings are given.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city's roof review (Local Law 24) lists this library as Not Solar Ready, with roof condition and roof age both unknown. The roof may need inspection, repair or replacement before solar, and none of the cost totals include a roof replacement. A roofer's quote is needed.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Have an engineer or roofer verify the usable roof area (size, pitch, direction, structure and shading) and enter it in the intake. Then solar and battery scenarios can be re-run. Real output on a pitched roof depends on its pitch and direction.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Scenario A, efficiency only: share of the goal is 21% to 59% (a 6.2% to 17.6% cut in annual use). It does not reach the goal. Upfront cost is $47,092 to $161,804 (typical range); net cost is the same because no incentive is counted. Simple payback is 4.1 to 49.1 years, a simple payback and not a full solar model. Budget strain is within budget. Outage hours are 0.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario A costs 9% to 32% of the $500,000 budget, so the estimated cost fits within the budget. The budget is a capital amount treated as one total upfront figure.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The two solar scenarios were not costed because they depend on a verified usable roof area. Whether the full path costs more than $500,000 cannot be said until that area is known. Meeting the goal may take more than the budget, and extending it would be your decision after comparing any gap with the savings.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Standard efficiency package: typical range $47,092 to $161,804; the median of similar NYC projects is about $103,039. Basis: 40,250 kWh saved a year (the middle of the 10-20% planning estimate) times $1.17 to $4.02 per kWh saved, the middle half of completed NYC public-sector LED and comprehensive projects since 2016 (NYSERDA data).
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Annual bill savings from efficiency are estimated at $3,296 to $11,419, using the New York commercial average price of about 19.8 to 24.2 cents per kWh, not this building's own tariff. At the median cost, simple payback is about 14 years.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The federal elective pay credit for governmental entities (retrieved 2026-10-19) is open for solar placed in service by 2027-12-31. Whether this library's owner qualifies is not confirmed. It is left out of net cost because no solar was costed.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The NYSERDA NY-Sun commercial solar incentive is uncertain: its dashboard could not be read automatically. It is left out of net cost. Check the dashboard in a browser.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: NYC's sustainable roof rules (Local Laws 92 and 94 of 2019) apply to existing buildings undergoing certain major roof renovations: the roof must carry solar, a green roof, or both. If the roof is replaced, this rule may apply. This is a rule, not an incentive.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Phase 0, confirm data and budget: confirm the floor area and address with the city's records, the year the roof was last replaced, bills, the capital budget for 2027 and the building's own Con Edison tariff.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 1, professional reviews: a structural PE or RA analysis and a roof condition survey that also verifies the usable roof area, since the roof cannot be certified from these records.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 2, efficiency measures: an energy audit, then the efficiency package for lighting, controls and cooling not already in place.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 3, permits and interconnection: Landmarks Preservation Commission review, Department of Buildings permits, a licensed electrician, FDNY rooftop access and the Con Edison interconnection application.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 4, solar installation, only after the roof area, structure and landmark approval are settled. Solar placed in service by 2027-12-31 is the federal credit window, which is tight.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 5, battery, commissioning and verification of savings against bills, once critical load and backup hours are set.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Critical loads named are reading room cooling and lighting. No battery was sized, because the critical load in kW (how much power at one moment) and the backup hours wanted were not given. No outage hours are available for the full path.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Efficiency alone (Scenario A) gives no backup power. Solar panels shut off in an outage without a battery, so any solar scenario also gives no backup without one.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The FEMA effective flood map shows zone X, an area of minimal flood hazard. Heat and winter-storm ratings were not looked up, and the 2015 preliminary flood map was not checked, so flood risk is not fully cleared.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city record flags this building as a landmark and it is in the Greenwich Village Historic District. A Landmarks Preservation Commission permit review is needed before any rooftop or exterior work. If the building is also on parkland, the Commission gives an advisory report and counsel should review parkland use. Parkland status was not confirmed.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The owning agency is NYPL according to the city's roof review, so its approval route should be confirmed. A structural PE or RA analysis, a roof condition survey, a licensed electrician, FDNY rooftop access approval and a Con Edison interconnection review are all required. The contact list at the end links to the offices.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

sections.title: Path to net-zero and learning resources

claims.text: Net-zero is not within reach on these records: gas heating remains outside an electricity goal, and the roof limits solar. A realistic order is efficiency first, then verified solar if the landmark review and roof allow it, then electrifying heating later.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The roof-area and array-size calculation refused to run (the calculate tool returned an error) because the roof is pitched. This is a decision from the roof rules, not a service that failed to answer. Because of it, solar size, solar output, solar savings and the two solar scenarios are missing until a verified usable roof area is entered. Re-run the plan once it is.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Entered values differ from city records: the city lists 421 Avenue of the Americas, not 425 6th Avenue, and its energy report shows 18,643 sq ft against 19,800 sq ft entered. The entered values are kept. Please confirm them.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Left blank in the intake: year the roof was replaced, roof condition, lighting and cooling type, controls, critical load, backup hours, heating fuel, electricity price and goal type. Claims that depend on them have lower confidence.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The electricity price is the New York commercial average, not this building's own tariff. Con Edison lists several general-service tariffs for New York City (effective 2025-02-01); the building's own tariff must be confirmed on a bill.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The incentive list is a curated register that a person keeps and the system verifies against official pages. NY-Sun status is uncertain and the federal credit eligibility is unconfirmed, so no incentive is counted.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Only the FEMA flood zone was read. Heat and winter-storm ratings were not checked, and the 2015 preliminary flood map was not checked.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Efficiency costs and savings are planning estimates with low confidence. Payback is a simple payback, not a full solar model, and all figures are estimate ranges, not promises or quotes.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

roadmap.footer_note: All figures are estimate ranges for planning. They are not quotes and not promises of savings.
roadmap.plain_answer: You asked whether the library can have rooftop solar and how to cut grid power 30% by 2030 on $500,000. Solar cannot be sized yet. The roof is pitched, the building is a landmark in a historic district, and the city's own roof review lists it as Not Solar Ready, so the sizing rules stopped until an engineer or roofer verifies the usable roof area. This was a decision from the rules, not missing data. Efficiency work alone is estimated to cut about 6% to 18% of your grid use, which is roughly a fifth to three-fifths of the goal. It would cost about $47,000 to $162,000, well within the budget, but it does not reach 30% on its own. The 268,331 kWh figure is electricity bought from the grid, and no existing solar or efficiency work was listed. The city lists the lot as 421 Avenue of the Americas and shows 18,643 square feet in its energy report, against your 425 6th Avenue and 19,800 square feet. Next: have an engineer or roofer verify the usable roof area, and start a Landmarks Preservation Commission review.
